one_liner: Connect your workspace to external tools and automate workflows through the Notion REST API.
auth_notes: Notion supports internal connection tokens, personal access tokens (bearer tokens), and OAuth 2.0 for public integrations.
access_notes: Developers can sign up for a free Notion account and immediately create internal connections or personal access tokens in the Developer portal at no cost.
api_notes: Covers pages, databases, users, comments, and blocks via the Notion REST API.
blocker_notes: Publicly available API with self-serve free developer access.

auth.quote: Notion supports three authentication models: are scoped to a single workspace and use a static API token. They’re ideal for custom automations and workflows — things like syncing data, sending notifications, or building internal dashboards. use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

access.guidance: Workspace Owner can create an internal connection directly in the Developer portal for free.
access.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Internal connections. Click Create a new connection, enter a connection name, and choose the workspace where the connection can be installed.

api.quote: With the REST API, you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more.

mcp.quote: Notion MCP lets an MCP client, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, connect to your Notion workspace through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

verdict.quote: For developers who want to build their own, Notion supports internal connections, public connections, and personal access tokens — all powered by the same REST API.

reasons.auth: Notion documents OAuth 2.0 and personal access tokens (static bearer tokens) for API authentication.
reasons.access: The API is available to all users with a free Notion account; no paid plan or approval is required to obtain credentials.
reasons.mcp: No official MCP server is published by Notion; only the REST API is documented.
reasons.verdict: All required documentation and free credentials are publicly available, enabling immediate development.
